title: Zenith Analytics - embeddings / reranking discovery
summary: Initial discovery to evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for embeddings + reranking use case. Discussed current stack (FAISS + custom vector store), throughput targets, embedding dimensionality and model choices, hybrid search (keyword + vector), security and compliance needs, and next steps for a POC and security review.
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options
SE to run throughput benchmark with sample dataset (10M docs) and share results
Send security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS docs) to Eleanor
Schedule deep-dive demo for indexing pipeline and routing (next week)
Customer to share sample queries + evaluation set for rerank metrics
action_items: Priya Shah (Redwood SE): run initial throughput benchmark using Zenith sample set and FAISS baseline by 2026-04-19
Alex Morgan (Redwood AE): send hosted/dedicated/private pricing and contract basics by 2026-04-14
Eleanor Park (CISO): review security pack and send questions by 2026-04-20
Marcus Lee (Zenith): share subset of production query logs + rerank evaluation set by 2026-04-16
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-12 15:00 UTC — 46 minutes. Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Zenith Head of Search), Ivy (ML Eng), Eleanor (CISO).

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick intro from our side. I'm Alex, account exec on the inference platform team, with Priya who's our SE.
00:10 Priya: hi all, Priya Shah, I run performance and infra for inference, happy to dig into embeddings and rerank.
00:16 Marcus: Marcus Lee here, we own search and recommendations at Zenith. we currently use an in-house FAISS cluster and a short list reranker, hoping to understand Redwood's hosted and dedicated options for embeddings and rerank.
00:28 Ivy: Ivy, ML eng, big on throughput and cost — we push a lot of requests during peak.
00:33 Eleanor: Eleanor, CISO, i'll mostly ask about data residency and key management.
00:38 Alex: great, maybe quick agenda — current stack, pain points, goals, then deep dive on integration patterns (vector DB, hybrid), and security. sound good?
00:45 Marcus: yep.
00:50 Priya: okay first, Marcus, can you run through your current flow and numbers?
00:55 Marcus: sure, currently we encode with our own 1536-dim model, store vectors in FAISS on-prem, hybrid search is a fuse of BM25 for candidate retrieval then vector rerank. peak qps about 450 qps across global nodes, typical latency requirement 50 to 150ms for first-pass, rerank can be a bit longer but we like sub-300ms end-to-end.
01:20 Alex: 450 qps is substantial. is that simultaneous per region or global?
01:25 Marcus: that's global, roughly 200 us-east, 150 eu, rest apac.
01:30 Ivy: also doc count is around 10 million active docs, with daily increments and frequent re-indexing for freshness.
01:38 Priya: good context. two immediate questions we usually see: embedding dimensionality choices and where to run embedding generation vs rerank — do you generate embeddings offline or at write-time?
01:48 Marcus: embeddings are generated at write time in our pipeline — we also re-embed when models update, which is a pain.
01:54 Alex: Redwood supports both hosted embedding generation and bring-your-own embeddings. for hosted, you can call our embeddings endpoint; for bring-your-own, we accept vectors and then Redwood handles the rerank/embedding storage and caching if desired.
02:07 Ivy: if we bring our own vectors (FAISS), do you integrate directly with existing vector DBs?
02:12 Priya: yes, we have adapters — we integrate commonly with Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate and we also support custom connectors. for on-prem FAISS we typically do a hybrid approach: keep FAISS as source-of-truth and Redwood runs rerank in a dedicated pool or via private deployment that can reach into your network.
02:31 Marcus: okay that hybrid flow sounds promising. what about throughput — can Redwood keep up with 450 qps and rerank latency constraints?
02:37 Priya: on Dedicated we provision GPU pools with predictable throughput; we size based on model (embedding dimension and model size) and sequence lengths. for 450 qps we usually recommend a few dedicated nodes with autoscale/burst enabled, or a hybrid where first-pass remains local and Redwood handles rerank.
02:54 Marcus: what's the typical per-request token cost and latency for rerank? say we use a 1536-dim embedding and a cross-encoder reranker.
03:02 Priya: latency for a cross-encoder rerank depends on model size — a distilled cross-encoder on GPU can be 30-80ms per request for short documents; cost depends on tokens but for embeddings+rerank the dominant cost is the cross-encoder inference. we can share benchmark numbers; we'll run a benchmark with your sample set.
03:18 Alex: also worth noting Redwood supports rerank in two modes: vector-sim score + lightweight rerank (fast) or full cross-encoder (higher quality, higher compute). you can trade quality vs cost.
03:30 Marcus: and about dimensionality — we currently use 1536 but we've seen vendors suggest 768 or 1024. any guidance?
03:36 Priya: larger dims often mean higher recall for some tasks, but also more storage and compute. for many rerank scenarios 768–1536 is common. model choice matters — some newer open models do 1024 or 1536; we can recommend quantization profiles and dimensionality tradeoffs after seeing your eval set.
03:51 Ivy: do you support quantized embeddings for storage to reduce cost?
03:54 Priya: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support quantization-friendly pipelines—down to int8 storage for vectors and optimized kernels in the runtime. Hosted also supports compressed vectors via our ingestion pipeline but there are some limits.
04:07 Marcus: hybrid search — we do BM25 first-pass and then embed top 1k and rerank. can Redwood handle batching those 1k candidates quickly?
04:15 Priya: batching is key. Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and KV cache; for a 1k candidate rerank we often do a two-stage process: use vector candidate reduction (dense retrieval) to 100–200 then cross-encoder on top-k. doing a full 1k cross-encoder is expensive.
04:30 Marcus: ok so we might need to tune first-pass thresholds.
04:34 Alex: another dimension is where the rerank runs — Hosted is easiest but if you need VPC or data residency, Dedicated or Private can be the right fit. Eleanor, any red flags on compliance?
04:45 Eleanor: SOC2 is table stakes. we also have data residency needs for EU customers; encryption at rest and customer-managed keys are required. audit logs and RBAC are important.
04:56 Priya: Redwood Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS/HSM, VPC peering, and audit logging. we can provide our security pack — SOC2 report, ISO certs, and a network architecture diagram.
05:07 Eleanor: great. also curious about data retention and the hosted ingestion pipeline — do you persist user inputs for model tuning?
05:13 Alex: by default hosted customers can opt-out of retention; for enterprise we do contractual terms to prevent data usage for model training. we'll include that in the security pack.
05:23 Marcus: what about vector DB integration specifics — if we keep FAISS on-prem and want Redwood to call into it for candidate retrieval, is there latency and security concerns?
05:33 Priya: yes, if Redwood needs to call into on-prem FAISS you'll want a Private deployment or a secure peering arrangement. For Dedicated we can set up a VPN/peering so the rerank cluster queries your FAISS via private network to avoid public ingress. latency depends on network — for us-east to on-prem colo it's usually fine but we'll bench it.
05:51 Ivy: can Redwood host the vector store for us? like move from FAISS to managed Milvus or Pinecone on your Dedicated infra?
05:58 Priya: we can host vector storage as part of the Redwood Dedicated offering; customers often use managed vector stores we support or Redwood's persistent store in Dedicated. moving from FAISS to managed store is a migration project, we provide tools and assistance.
06:10 Marcus: competition — we've evaluated Pinecone and Milvus. Pinecone had better managed offering but cost was high. how does Redwood compare to Pinecone + custom rerank?
06:20 Alex: Redwood bundles the inference runtime with orchestration and routing; instead of two vendors you'll get a unified SLO for rerank performance and more cost controls (batching, quantization). pricing will depend on throughput and model choices.
06:32 Ivy: what about open models — can we run embeddings from Llama2-like open models?
06:36 Priya: yes, Dedicated and Private can run open models you prefer; Hosted has curated model catalog with verified performance. you can also bring-your-own model weights for Private.
06:46 Marcus: on the POC — can we run Redwood hosted for a small pilot (100k docs) to validate quality then scale to Dedicated?
06:53 Alex: yes that's a common path: start hosted to validate, then Dedicated for production throughput and compliance. we'll include pricing for both and options to migrate.
07:00 Marcus: for the POC we want accuracy metrics — precision@k, MRR, latency P95.
07:05 Priya: we'll run those benchmarks and produce a spreadsheet with exact numbers vs your baseline FAISS+local reranker.
07:12 Ivy: regarding instrumentation: do you provide per-token cost breakdown and per-route latency?
07:16 Alex: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards, tracing, and token-level cost breakdowns. we'll give you a demo.
07:23 Marcus: okay security/contract questions — for Dedicated is there a minimum commit?
07:27 Alex: Dedicated has reserved capacity contracts, monthly or annual commits; we'll outline options in the pricing. for Private on-prem we have enterprise licensing.
07:36 Eleanor: also want to confirm SSO — we use SAML and need SCIM provisioning.
07:41 Priya: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC.
07:45 Marcus: anything else about latency when using cross-region routing?
07:49 Priya: Redwood Smart Routing can route requests to nearest region or fall back; there is some added routing latency but it's small compared to inference time. we can pin traffic to specific regions for strict latency SLOs.
07:59 Marcus: curious about cost optimization — you mentioned batching and KV caching, any examples?
08:05 Priya: yes, we do intelligent batching to improve GPU utilization and KV caching for prefix reuse. for rerank workloads with overlapping queries we often reduce compute by caching intermediate embeddings and using smaller cross-encoders for short contexts. we'll share an optimize playbook.
08:21 Ivy: for our eval — should we send dense vectors or raw text to Redwood?
08:25 Priya: either works. sending raw text lets Redwood generate embeddings and gives you simpler workflow; sending dense vectors avoids re-embedding and can be cheaper if you already compute them. we'll test both in the POC.
08:37 Marcus: any pitfalls for migrating from FAISS?
08:40 Priya: migration issues are usually indexing time, dimensionality mismatches, and similarity metric differences (cosine vs dot). we help with scripts to reindex and test buckets.
08:49 Alex: okay to recap next steps? we'll send pricing, security pack, SE will run benchmark, customer will share evaluation artifacts, and schedule deep-dive next week.
08:58 Marcus: yes, sounds good.
09:02 Eleanor: I'll look at the security docs once you send them.
09:06 Ivy: I'll prepare the eval set and logs.
09:10 Alex: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the links.
09:15 Marcus: thanks.

--- End of transcript notes: There's occasional transcription noise (names, acronyms). Links referenced: /pricing (sent after), security-pack.zip (to be shared), benchmark-spreadsheet (to be shared).
